## What I did

- Add a builder-agnostic ModuleGraph / ModuleNode type to core builder types so builders can expose dependency graph updates
- Implement Vite module graph conversion and an onModuleGraphChange subscription API in @storybook/builder-vite
- Add tests for module graph conversion, listener registration, debounce behavior, and cleanup on bail()

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Test assertion doesn't match implementation behavior.**

The test expects `watcher.off` to be called with `'change'` event (line 332), but the implementation registers the handler on `'all'` event (index.ts:161). The `bail()` function calls `off('change', ...)` which won't actually remove the `'all'` handler.

This test will pass with the current mock setup due to how the fake watcher isolates events, but it documents incorrect expected behavior. The implementation should be fixed to use consistent event names (see review comment on index.ts).

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/builders/builder-vite/src/index.test.ts` around lines 321 - 333, The
test and implementation disagree on event names: onModuleGraphChange registers a
handler on the watcher's 'all' event but bail() removes 'change' handlers;
update the implementation so the same event name is used everywhere. Locate the
onModuleGraphChange function and the bail function (symbols:
onModuleGraphChange, bail) and change the registration/removal to the same event
(either use 'all' for both registration and off call, or register on 'change'
and off('change', ...) consistently), and ensure watcher.off is invoked with the
exact handler reference that was passed to watcher.on so the listener is
actually removed.
```

</details>

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Event name mismatch: handler registered on `'all'` but removed from `'change'`.**

The watcher handler is registered on `'all'` event (line 161) but `bail()` attempts to remove it from `'change'` event. This means the handler won't actually be detached, causing:
1. Potential memory leak (handler stays attached)
2. Handler continues firing after bail (though listeners are cleared, so no callbacks execute)
3. If `start()` is called again, orphaned handlers accumulate

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 export async function bail(): Promise<void> {
   if (watcherChangeHandler) {
-    server?.watcher.off('change', watcherChangeHandler);
+    server?.watcher.off('all', watcherChangeHandler);
     watcherChangeHandler = undefined;
   }
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
export async function bail(): Promise<void> {
  if (watcherChangeHandler) {
    server?.watcher.off('all', watcherChangeHandler);
    watcherChangeHandler = undefined;
  }
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/builders/builder-vite/src/index.ts` around lines 120 - 124, The bail()
function is removing watcherChangeHandler from the wrong event ('change'); since
the handler was registered on the 'all' event, update the removal to use the
same event name so the handler is detached properly: in bail() locate the
server?.watcher.off('change', watcherChangeHandler) call and change it to
off('all', watcherChangeHandler) (keep the watcherChangeHandler guard and set
watcherChangeHandler = undefined afterwards) so the handler registered by the
start/registration logic is actually removed.
```

</details>

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `buildModuleGraph()` currently writes the entire module graph to stdout via `console.log`. This will be very noisy in normal Storybook dev sessions and can significantly slow down large graphs. Please remove these logs, or route them through the existing Storybook/Vite logger behind an explicit debug flag.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests removal or proper routing of console.log calls through a logger/debug flag.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: The watcher listener is registered with `server.watcher.on('all', watcherChangeHandler)`, but `bail()` removes it with `off('change', watcherChangeHandler)`. This won't actually unsubscribe, so the handler can keep running after shutdown and leak across restarts/tests. Use the same event name for `off()` as used for `on()` (or keep separate handlers per event).

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies the same event name mismatch bug (on 'all' vs off 'change') and requests fix.
